'''Jesús Guillera''' (31 December 1955 – 9 February 2026) was a Spanish mathematician who specialised in [[number theory]], best known for his work on Ramanujan-type series for calculating the mathematical constant [[Pi|π]]. Largely self-taught in advanced mathematics, he later earned a doctorate from the University of Zaragoza and since then published extensively on hypergeometric identities, WZ-pairs, and related topics in analytic number theory.<ref name=" article1"> {{cite news |last= Oto |first= J. |date= 6 April 2015 |title= Una mente maravillosa |url= https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/noticias/aragon/mente-maravillosa_1016667.html |trans-title= A beautiful mind |publisher= el Periόdico de Aragόn|language= Spanish |access-date= 10 August 2025}} </ref>

== Education and career ==
Guillera obtained a Bachelor of Science in Physics from the [[University of Zaragoza]] in 1979. For much of his career, he taught physics and mathematics at secondary schools in the province of Zaragoza.<ref name=" article2">{{cite news  |last= Ansede |first= Manuel| date=2 April 2015 |title=A life with pi | url=https://english.elpais.com/elpais/2015/04/01/inenglish/1427892395_607702.html | publisher= El Paίs |access-date= 10 August 2025 }}</ref> In 2002, Guillera took a medical leave from teaching due to stress and began to devote himself to the study of mathematics, focusing on studying the number [[Pi|π]].<ref name=" article3">{{cite web |last= Cotera | first= Lara | date=5 April 2015  | title=Las once fórmulas de Pi de una mente maravillosa | url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/aragon/2015/04/05/las-once-formulas-de-pi-de-una-mente-maravillosa-245580.html |trans-title= The eleven formulas of Pi from a beautiful mind | publisher= Heraldo de Aragόn |language= Spanish |access-date= 10 August 2025}}</ref>

Working independently and without formal academic affiliation, Guillera discovered previously unpublished formulas that drew international attention from the mathematical community.<ref name="article2"/> In 2007, he earned his PhD in number theory from the University of Zaragoza under the supervision of [[Eva Gallardo]] and [[Wadim Zudilin]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=124102}}</ref> His [[thesis]] received the distinction ''cum laude'' and was awarded the Extraordinary Prize.<ref name="article1"/> Guillera had since served as a researcher in the Department of Mathematics at the University of Zaragoza.<ref>[https://anamat.unizar.es/jguillera University of Zaragoza – Jesús Guillera]</ref>

== Mathematical work ==
Unlike many mathematicians who spend decades working, often doing their best work when young, Guillera has only been active since the age of 47 when he retired for medical reasons from high-school teaching. Since 2002, he has published over 40 works, and has been cited over 1200 times.<ref>{{Google scholar ID|id=p13LwaoAAAAJ}}</ref><ref>{{ZbMATH|guillera.jesus}}</ref> His work has been described in some news articles,<ref name="article1"/><ref name="article2"/><ref name="article4"/> and some have argued that his talent can be compared to [[Srinivasa Ramanujan]].<ref name="article2"/><ref name=" article5"> {{cite news |last= Sacristán |first= Enrique |date= 4 June 2016 |title= Ramanujan creía que una diosa le dictaba sus fórmulas mientras dormía |url= https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/noticias/aragon/mente-maravillosa_1016667.html |trans-title= Ramanujan believed that a goddess dictated his formulas to him while he slept |publisher= Agencia Sinc |language= Spanish |access-date= 11 August 2025}} </ref> "“Guillera is our own Ramanujan,” says Javier Cilleruelo, a member of Spain’s Institute of Mathematical Sciences (ICMAT)",<ref name="article2"/> while [[Doron Zeilberger]] described him as "My great hero Jesús Guillera, a 21st-century incarnation of Ramanujan".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Doron Zeilberger's 191st Opinion |url=https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~zeilberg/Opinion191.html |access-date= 11 August 2025 |website=sites.math.rutgers.edu}}</ref>

Guillera is known for his contributions to the study of Ramanujan-type series for calculating the number π.<ref name=" article4">{{cite web |last= Poblaciόn| first= Alfonso J.| date=30 April 2019 | title=Las asombrosas fórmulas matemáticas desarrolladas por un profesor español |  url=https://www.abc.es/ciencia/abci-asombrosas-formulas-matematicas-desarrolladas-profesor-espanol-201904290221_noticia.html|  trans-title= The amazing mathematical formulas developed by a Spanish professor |publisher= ABC |language= Spanish |access-date= 10 August 2025}}</ref> In 2002, he discovered several new series of this kind.<ref name= "journal1"> {{cite journal |last1= Guillera |first1= Jesús |date= 2002 |title= Some binomial series obtained by the WZ-method |url= https://doi.org/10.1016/S0196-8858(02)00034-9 |journal= Advances in Applied Mathematics |volume= 29 |issue= 4 |pages= 599–603 |doi=10.1016/S0196-8858(02)00034-9 |arxiv= math/0503345  }} </ref> Many of his formulas initially lacked formal proofs; over time, several were proven using the [[Wilf–Zeilberger pair]] method.<ref name= "journal2"> {{cite journal |last1= Guillera |first1= Jesús |date= 2010 |title= On WZ-pairs which prove Ramanujan series |url= https://doi.org/10.1007/s11139-010-9238-1 |journal= The Ramanujan Journal |volume= 22 |issue= 3 |pages= 249–259 |doi= 10.1007/s11139-010-9238-1 |arxiv= 0904.0406 }} </ref> He has also contributed to developing a general methodology for generating new Ramanujan-type series.<ref name= "journal3"> {{cite journal |last1= Guillera |first1= Jesús |date= 2020 |title= A method for proving Ramanujan's series for 1/π |url= https://doi.org/10.1007/s11139-018-0113-9 |journal= The Ramanujan Journal |volume= 52 | pages= 421–431 |doi= 10.1007/s11139-018-0113-9 | arxiv=1807.07394 }} </ref>

His research collaborations have included work with mathematicians such as [[Wadim Zudilin]], and he has received support from figures like Doron Zeilberger.<ref name="article4"/>

== Death ==
Guillera died on 9 February 2026, at the age of 70.<ref>{{cite web |title=Welcome to Jesús Guillera web page |url=https://anamat.unizar.es/jguillera/ |website=anamat.unizar.es |access-date=13 February 2026}}</ref>
